# 2 Kings Chapter 20 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 241v–242r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_020_page_481.jpg, 2KI_020_page_482.jpg

---

**20:1** In-those days Chizkiyahu was-sick [choleh] unto-death [la-mut]. And-came to-him Yesha'yahu son of-Amots the-prophet and-said to-him: Thus says YHWH: Command [tsav] your-house [le-veytekha], for you [are] dying [met] and-will-not live [ve-lo tichyeh].

**20:2** And-he-turned [vayassev] his-face to the-wall [ha-qir] and-prayed [vayitpallel] to YHWH, saying:

**20:3** Please [annah], YHWH, remember [zekhor], please, that I-have-walked [hithalakhti] before-you [lefaneykha] in-truth [be-emet] and-with-a-whole heart [u-ve-lev shalem], and-the-good [ha-tov] in-your-eyes I-have-done ['asiti]. And-wept [vayevke] Chizkiyahu a-great weeping [bekhi gadol].

**20:4** And-it-was [vayehi] — Yesha'yahu had-not gone-out [lo yatsa'] [from] the-middle court [chatser ha-tiykhonah] — and-the-word of-YHWH came [hayah] to-him, saying:

**20:5** Return [shuv] and-say to Chizkiyahu, leader [nagid] of-my-people: Thus says YHWH, God of-David your-father: I-have-heard [shamati] your-prayer [tefillatekha]; I-have-seen [ra'iti] your-tears [dim'atekha]. Behold, I-am-healing-you [rofekha]; on-the-third day you-shall-go-up [ta'aleh] to-the-house of-YHWH.

**20:6** And-I-will-add [ve-yasafti] to-your-days fifteen years [chamesh esreh shanah], and-from-the-hand [mi-kaph] of-the-king of-Ashur I-will-deliver-you [atsiylekha] and-this city, and-I-will-defend [ve-gannoti] upon this city for-my-sake [le-ma'ani] and-for-the-sake of-David my-servant ['avdi].

**20:7** And-said Yesha'yahu: Take [qechu] a-cake of-figs [develat te'enim]. And-they-took [vayiqchu] and-placed-it [vayasimu] upon the-boil [ha-shechin], and-he-lived [vayechi].

**20:8** And-said Chizkiyahu to Yesha'yahu: What [is] the-sign [ha-ot] that YHWH will-heal-me [yirpa'eni] and-that-I-shall-go-up on-the-third day to-the-house of-YHWH?

**20:9** And-said Yesha'yahu: This [is] the-sign [ha-ot] for-you from YHWH, that YHWH will-do the-thing [ha-davar] that he-has-spoken: Shall the-shadow [ha-tsel] go-forward [halakh] ten steps [eser ma'alot], or shall-it-return [yashuv] backward [achoranit] ten steps?

**20:10** And-said Chizkiyahu: It-is-light [naqal] for-the-shadow to-extend [lintot] ten steps. No [lo], let-the-shadow return [yashuv] backward ten steps.

**20:11** And-called [vayiqra'] Yesha'yahu the-prophet to YHWH, and-he-returned [vayashev] the-shadow on-the-steps [ba-ma'alot] that it-had-gone-down [yaredah] on-the-steps [be-ma'alot] of-Achaz, backward [achoranit] ten steps.

**20:12** At-that time Berodakh-Bal'adan son of-Bal'adan, king of-Bavel, sent letters [sefarim] and-a-gift [minchah] to Chizkiyahu, for he-had-heard that Chizkiyahu had-been-sick [choleh].

**20:13** And-listened [vayishma'] to-them Chizkiyahu, and-showed-them [vayar'em] all [et kol] the-house of-his-treasure [bet nekhotoh] — the-silver [ha-kesef] and-the-gold [ha-zahav] and-the-spices [ha-besamim] and-the-good oil [shemen ha-tov] and-the-house of-his-weapons [bet kelav] and-all that-was-found [nimtsa'] in-his-treasuries [be-otsrotav]. There-was-not a-thing [davar] that Chizkiyahu did-not show-them [lo her'am] in-his-house [be-veyto] and-in-all his-dominion [memshalto].

**20:14** And-came Yesha'yahu the-prophet to the-king Chizkiyahu and-said to-him: What did-these men say, and-from-where [me-ayin] did-they-come to-you? And-said Chizkiyahu: From-a-far land [me-erets rechoquah] they-came, from-Bavel.

**20:15** And-he-said: What did-they-see [ra'u] in-your-house? And-said Chizkiyahu: All that [is] in-my-house they-saw [ra'u]. There-is-not a-thing [davar] in-my-treasuries [be-otsrotay] that I-did-not show-them [lo hir'itim].

**20:16** And-said Yesha'yahu to Chizkiyahu: Hear [shema'] the-word of-YHWH:

**20:17** Behold, days [are] coming [ba'im] when-all that [is] in-your-house, and-that your-fathers have-stored-up [otseru] to this day, shall-be-carried [yinnase'] to-Bavel. Not a-thing [davar] shall-be-left [yivvater], says [amar] YHWH.

**20:18** And-from your-sons [u-mi-baneykha] who go-forth [yets'u] from-you, whom you-shall-beget [tolid], they-shall-take [yiqquchu], and-they-shall-be eunuchs [sarisim] in-the-palace [be-heykhal] of-the-king of-Bavel.

**20:19** And-said Chizkiyahu to Yesha'yahu: Good [tov] [is] the-word of-YHWH that you-have-spoken [dibbarta]. And-he-said: Is-it-not [ha-lo'] [so], if [im] peace [shalom] and-truth [emet] shall-be [yihyeh] in-my-days?

**20:20** And-the-rest of-the-acts [divrey] of-Chizkiyahu, and-all his-might [gevurato], and-how he-made [asah] the-pool [ha-berekhah] and-the-conduit [ha-te'alah] and-brought [vayave'] the-water into-the-city — are-they-not written in-the-scroll of-the-chronicles of-the-kings of-Yehudah?

**20:21** And-lay-down [vayishkav] Chizkiyahu with his-fathers, and-became-king [vayimlokh] Menasheh his-son in-his-place [tachtav].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "Command your house":** The verb *tsav* (command, set in order) implies both making a will and putting one's affairs in order. Isaiah delivers a death sentence — not a prognosis but a divine pronouncement. The finality is absolute: "you are dying and will not live."

**v.3 — *be-emet u-ve-lev shalem*:** "In truth and with a whole heart" — Hezekiah's appeal is to his covenantal faithfulness, his *emet* (truth/reliability) before YHWH. The "whole heart" (*lev shalem*) is the Deuteronomic ideal — undivided loyalty. His weeping is recorded without comment; the narrator lets the emotion stand.

**v.11 — *ma'alot Achaz*:** "Steps of Ahaz" — likely a sundial-stairway or stepped structure built by Ahaz. The shadow moves backward on the very steps Hezekiah's idolatrous father built. The son's sign of life operates on the father's architecture of death — a quiet irony.

**v.13 — *bet nekhotoh*:** "House of his treasure" — *nekhotoh* is a rare word, possibly related to "precious things" or "storehouse." Hezekiah's comprehensive tour — showing *everything* — is narrated with a note of excess. The repeated emphasis ("there was not a thing he did not show them") signals folly.

**v.19 — Hezekiah's response:** "Good is the word of YHWH" followed by "if peace and truth shall be in my days?" — one of the most debated verses in Kings. Is Hezekiah accepting the judgment with humility, or is he selfishly relieved that the catastrophe will come after his death? The Hebrew is ambiguous, and the narrator offers no commentary. The reader must judge.

**v.20 — The pool and the conduit:** The Siloam tunnel inscription (discovered 1880) confirms this engineering feat — a 533-meter tunnel cut through solid rock to bring water from the Gihon Spring inside Jerusalem's walls. It is one of the rare cases where an archaeological find directly confirms a biblical detail.

*— EMET*
